summary: Mecetronium (mecetronium ethylsulfate / mecetronium etilsulfate) is a quaternary ammonium antiseptic and preservative used as a component of alcohol-based surgical hand disinfectants and hand rubs (for example combined with ethanol and isopropanol in products such as Sterillium). As a cationic surfactant it disrupts microbial cell membranes, providing topical antimicrobial action with some residual antibacterial activity that persists after the alcohol has evaporated. It is for external/topical use only on hands and skin and is not used systemically. Possible skin irritation or contact dermatitis can occur; products are flammable while wet, and eyes, mucous membranes and ingestion must be avoided. Mecetronium is NOT an FDA-approved drug substance and is used predominantly in Europe as an antiseptic ingredient.
indications: Hygienic and surgical hand disinfection (as a component of alcohol-based hand rubs)

dosage.d: Apply the alcohol-based hand rub containing mecetronium to hands and forearms, keeping skin wet for the full prescribed contact time, and rub until dry
dosage.n: Follow the specific product's contact time (often several minutes for surgical antisepsis)

dosage.d: Apply sufficient volume to cover both hands, rub in for the labeled time (commonly ~30 seconds) until dry
dosage.n: Do not rinse; allow to air-dry

dosage.d: Apply to intact skin and allow the prescribed contact/drying time

admin: External use only - apply to intact skin/hands; do not swallow
Use sufficient volume to keep skin wet for the labeled contact time, then allow to air-dry; do not rinse off prematurely
Keep away from flames, sparks and heat until fully dry, as alcohol-based products are flammable
Avoid contact with eyes, mucous membranes, open wounds and broken skin
Do not apply to large denuded areas or use on neonates' skin except where the specific product permits
moa: Mecetronium is a quaternary ammonium compound that acts as a cationic surfactant. Its positively charged head group is attracted to the negatively charged microbial cell surface; it inserts into and disrupts the cytoplasmic membrane, denatures proteins and causes leakage of intracellular contents, leading to cell death. This gives broad antibacterial activity and contributes a residual (persistent) antimicrobial effect on the skin after the co-formulated alcohols have evaporated.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to mecetronium or other quaternary ammonium compounds or formulation components
Application to the eyes or mucous membranes
relative: Pre-existing irritant or allergic contact dermatitis on the hands
Application to broken or extensively damaged skin
monitor: Skin irritation and signs of contact dermatitis

preg: Mecetronium is used topically as an antiseptic with minimal systemic absorption, so systemic fetal exposure is expected to be negligible. External hand and skin disinfection is generally considered acceptable during pregnancy when used as directed.
lact: Systemic absorption from topical use is minimal and clinically significant transfer into breast milk is not expected. External hand/skin disinfection is acceptable during breastfeeding; avoid applying to the breast/nipple and ensure hands are dry before infant contact.
renal: Not applicable - topical antiseptic with minimal systemic absorption; no renal considerations or dose adjustment.
hepatic: Not applicable - topical antiseptic with minimal systemic absorption; no hepatic considerations or dose adjustment.

moderate: Anionic surfactants (e.g., ordinary soaps) - can neutralize the cationic antimicrobial activity if used concurrently on the same skin
Other topical irritants - additive skin irritation
minor: Other cationic or alcohol-based skin products - generally compatible but may add to drying/irritation
interactions.alcohol: Co-formulated with ethanol/isopropanol; the product is flammable while wet - allow to dry fully before exposure to flame or smoking.

common: Mild skin irritation at application site
serious: Allergic or severe irritant contact dermatitis
emergency: Severe allergic reaction (swelling, hives, difficulty breathing)
Chemical burn/severe irritation of eye after accidental exposure

monitoring: Skin condition with repeated use - dryness, irritation, dermatitis
Signs of contact sensitization in frequent users (e.g., healthcare workers)

Typically present in alcohol-based hand rubs alongside ethanol and isopropanol (e.g., Sterillium) where it provides residual antibacterial activity

External/topical use only - minimal systemic absorption, so systemic PK is largely N/A

missed: Not applicable in the usual sense - this is an as-needed topical antiseptic rather than a scheduled systemic medicine; simply apply when hand or skin disinfection is required.
overdose: Topical overuse mainly causes skin dryness and irritation; treat by stopping use and applying emollients. Accidental ingestion of alcohol-based product can cause alcohol toxicity and GI/mucosal irritation - do not induce vomiting, give supportive care and seek medical/poison-center advice. For eye contact, rinse copiously with water and obtain ophthalmologic review if irritation persists.
